conventions: Every one-English-word fusion in this chapter is recorded `aligned`, never `noncompositional`: waw+lo -> *neither* (7.4, 7.9, 7.13, 7.19) and -> *nor* (7.11, twice), waw+al -> *nor* (7.12), min+qarob -> *shortly* (7.8), be+chuts -> *without* and min+bayit -> *within* (7.15), be+suffix -> *therein* and al-ken -> *therefore* (7.20). Rules 6, 30 and 35 do not settle the status, and the corpus splits almost evenly on the identical constructions (waw+lo -> *neither*: 88 aligned against 98 noncompositional; -> *nor*: 126 against 54; be+suffix -> *therein*: 27 against 24), so the chapter chose one and held it throughout. Heads follow rule 35: the negative for a fused negative, otherwise the morpheme carrying the lexeme.

The frozen first-person suffix of adonai is `unrepresented` (7.2 s008, 7.5 s004): the ASV writes *the Lord Jehovah* with no pronoun answering to it, and the supplied *the* belongs to adonai's own unit under rule 15 rather than to the suffix. BSB counts this suffix represented in both verses; that is a convention difference and not a correction.

ASV italics are placed in this chapter by asking what the italicized word completes, not by rule 7 alone. An italic that completes the English phrase rendering one substantive joins that substantive's unit and is not added: *a day of* tumult and *of* joyful shouting (7.7 s015, s018) and secret *place* (7.22 s010), which is how the unitalicized *an unclean thing* (7.19 s011, 7.20 s025), *detestable things* (7.20 s013) and *holy places* (7.24 s016) are placed too. An italic that instead supplies a predicate for a clause whose Hebrew has no verb (*shall remain*, 7.11, rule 20) or a connective standing between two nominals the Hebrew joins asyndetically (*and*, 7.20, rule 42) answers to no morpheme and is `added`. These are the chapter's only two added units.
report: Checked all 43 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by what the ASV wrote, not by two analyses of one construction: the waw takes Moreover, And, but, also, although, Wherefore or As for as written; the article is aligned wherever a *the*, a relative or a determiner stands for it and unrepresented where the ASV writes none (7.10 pride, 7.11 Violence, 7.14 all, 7.17 All hands); every unrepresented preposition (7.4 spare thee, 7.13 alive, 7.14 blown the trumpet) is rule 40 recasting.

The near-duplicate judgment formulae agree morpheme for morpheme. 7.3 and 7.8 both fuse the kaph into *according to* (rule 30), give *I will bring* to natan, *upon* to al, and leave the object marker unrepresented. 7.4 and 7.9 both give *mine* to the suffix and *eye* to the noun, fuse waw plus lo into *neither*, head *have pity* on *pity* (rule 44), and split *the midst* / *of thee* by rules 29 and 19. The divergences are ones the Hebrew licenses: 7.9 writes no alayik after tachos and closes with a participial predicate, so no copula is supplied there.

The supplied-article method is uniform across every construct chain: count the ASV's *the*s, give each present article the one standing before its own word, put the rest on the constructs. 7.2, 7.19, 7.21, 7.24 and 7.27 all follow it; 7.16 writes only one *the* and gives it to the article before *valleys*; 7.12, 7.13 and 7.14 all put the phrase's single supplied *the* on the construct hamon, while 7.11 differs only because the ASV writes a possessive there.

Read the chapter past the table where the lemma keying is blind, namely the two added units and the five ASV-italic sites. They agree with each other: an italic completing one substantive's English phrase stays in that substantive's unit (7.7 *a day of* tumult, *of* joyful shouting; 7.22 secret *place*; matching the unitalicized *an unclean thing* at 7.19 and 7.20 and *holy places* at 7.24), while an italic supplying a predicate for a clause whose Hebrew has no verb (7.11 *shall remain*, rule 20) or a connective between two asyndetic nominals (7.20 *and*, rule 42) is added. Those two are the chapter's only added units and both are correct.

BSB: all 12 disagreements are documented convention differences, none an error. 7.1 le-emor is rule 27. 7.4 alayik, 7.13 ba and 7.14 ba are rule 40 recastings, which rule 21 names as the usual source of prophetic-book disagreement since BSB attaches the preposition to its phrase. 7.2 and 7.5 are the frozen suffix of adonai, for which the ASV writes no pronoun. The four Td cases (7.10, 7.11, 7.14, 7.17) are phrases the ASV writes with no *the*. 7.13 chayyatam and its suffix are collapsed by the ASV's recasting to *they be yet alive*, which writes no word for *life*. No accepted edge was changed.

One note-level defect, recorded here rather than patched: EZK.7.7 s019 cites rule 19's construct recasting for *upon the mountains*, but MACULA tags both hed (Ncmsa) and harim (Ncmpa) absolute, so the phrase is juxtaposition and the supplied *upon* is rule 33's adverbial-accusative supply, exactly as *as water* (7.17), *with sackcloth* (7.18), *with desolation* (7.27) and *of violence* (7.23) are placed. The unit's edges and head are identical under either rule, so a full-verse patch would change only a citation.
The log had 0 conventions against 63 repeating notes; three are recorded now. The largest is the fusion-status choice, which the contract leaves open and the corpus splits nearly evenly on.

No promotions. The one construction the contract had not met is 7.20's waw taking *As for* in an object-fronting clause with no object marker present (rule 16's *as for* clause presupposes a marker). It is a single occurrence with no corpus evidence in this packet, and the verse pass already named the competing reading under rule 8, so a rule built on it would be the weak kind this project has had to live with. A later chapter meeting it again, with LEMMA=waw TARGET='^as for' in hand, is what should settle it.
